summary: A pill-shaped filter chip: a tap toggles its 0/1 `selected` variable (then runs any extra `onClick` actions), and the selected face (filled with `color`) fades in over the plain one. A screen reader hears the label and Selected or Not selected, which follows the value; the 32 dp pill sits in a 48 dp tall touch target.

selected.doc: 0/1. Bind a document variable to read or preset it ("@travel"); omitted, the chip keeps its own, starting unselected

color.doc: The selected face; its label is onPrimary

onClick.doc: Extra actions run on every tap after the toggle of `selected` (hostNamedAction, valueFloatChange, ...), e.g. [{"type": "hostNamedAction", "name": "kitchenLight"}]. Omitted: the tap only toggles `selected`

pitfalls: State colours without colour expressions: the two faces are stacked in one clipped box (same padding, same text, so the same size) and the top one's graphicsLayer alpha is the 0/1 state
Chips wrap their label: put them in a row (or several rows) with spacedBy; a `flow` ignores spacedBy
The label is one line with an ellipsis (maxLines 1): in a slot narrower than the label it ends in … instead of wrapping and being clipped by the pill
Selecting cross-fades: the selected face's graphicsLayer alpha is the animated value {"value": "@selected", "anim": 0.2} (paint time; mono strips the motion)
`onClick` actions run after the toggle: an app reading the exported `selected` on a hostNamedAction sees the new state

Touch target: 8 dp of padding above and below the 32 dp pill make the chip 48 dp tall, all of it clickable; leave no extra vertical space between rows of chips (the padding is the gap). The width is the pill's: a label under about 20 dp ("On", one or two letters) leaves the target under 48 dp wide (no widthIn: the players disagree on it)

Accessibility: the chip carries the label (contentDescription), the state (stateDescription, Selected or Not selected) and the click. The state is cut from "Not selectedSelected    " by textSubtext at 12 * selected and trimmed, in the global section of a 0-size canvas placed before the chip, so it follows a bound variable at run time. About 150 B per call, and the named text ops keep it from compiling to a pattern
